overrides.name: unifi_dynamic_dns
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. Two renames read from the resource conversion code: id from _id, and password from the SDK's x_password, which the policy also marks sensitive so the secret guard stays satisfied. site is provider-owned rather than the SDK's site_id — dynamicDNSToModel takes the site name as a parameter and site_id is never read or written here, so matching on the name would have bound the wrong field. Seven SDK fields are omitted: the four attr_ bookkeeping flags, site_id, and custom_service and options, none of which the released schema ever exposed. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_firewall_group
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. Three renames read from the resource conversion code: id from _id, type from group_type, members from group_members. site is provider-owned rather than the SDK's site_id — firewallGroupToModel sets it from a parameter, and the update path's SiteID assignment writes the site name into that field rather than reading it. Descriptions are grafted back to plain, the second surface to need that. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_firewall_zone
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the catalog and policy. Nine of the twelve SDK fields are controller bookkeeping the released schema never exposed and the policy omits by name. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_site
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the catalog and policy. Two renames read from the resource conversion code: the SDK stores the description as desc and the ID as _id. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_ap_group
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. id renames to the SDK's _id. site is provider-owned, not the SDK's site_id: the site name reaches the model as a function parameter and site_id is never read or written here, so matching on the name would have bound the wrong field. device_macs keeps its hwtypes.MACAddress element type, which neither referee can see, and its plan modifier moved to unifi/planmodifiers to be reachable from generated code. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_firewall_policy
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the catalog and policy and matches the released schema attribute for attribute, including both nested shapes. Admission waits on a campaign run, which is the only thing that can say whether the generated resource behaves as the hand-written one did.

overrides.name: unifi_wireguard_peer
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy with no omissions: every SDK field is served. id renames to _id, and site is provider-owned — this SDK struct carries no site_id at all, so the site name only ever arrives as a parameter. allowed_ips keeps its empty-list default, transcribed as a custom default because ListDefault has no static form in the specification. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_wlan
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the catalog and policy: 55 released attributes over 109 SDK fields, ten renames read from the resource conversion code, a mac_filter grouping, a schedule block bound to schedule_with_duration rather than the SDK field of the same name, one invented block member, and 54 named omissions. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_account
overrides.migration: Served by the generated schema without a policy of its own. deprecatedAccountResource embeds radiusUserResource and calls its Schema, adding only a DeprecationMessage, so migrating unifi_radius_user migrated this surface in the same edit. It has no bootstrap, policy or generated package, and it must not acquire one: a second policy over the same SDK struct would be a second source of truth for one schema. The baseline projection reads it as a registered resource and compares it against the released contract like any other, which is what says the alias still inherits what it did. Admission waits on the same campaign run as unifi_radius_user.

overrides.name: unifi_bgp
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. Three renames read from the resource conversion code: id from _id, config from frr_bgpd_config and upload_file_name from uploaded_file_name, none of which a name match would have found. Five of the ten SDK fields are omitted: site_id and the four attr_ bookkeeping flags. Four of the nine released attributes are provider-owned rather than derived — site, and asn, router_id and peers, which the controller never stores: modelToBGP renders them into the FRR config string and bgpToModel preserves them from state rather than parsing them back. peers is the estate's only provider-owned nested attribute, so its members are written in specification form and its one validator was transcribed by hand, which the deriver now says rather than reporting it as omitted. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_client_qos_rate
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. The surface fronts the SDK's ClientGroup, not a struct of its own name, so the bootstrap is derived from that type. id renames to _id; site is provider-owned rather than site_id, which this resource never reads or writes. Both rate defaults are int64default.StaticInt64(-1), transcribed by hand because the behaviour deriver stops at the unary minus rather than guessing. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_power_supervisor
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the catalog and policy, spreading the SDK Settings struct into the three duration attributes the released schema presents at the top level. Admission waits on a campaign run.

overrides.name: unifi_radius_user
overrides.migration: Schema compiles from the bootstrap and policy. Three renames read from the resource conversion code: id from _id, password from x_password — sensitive, as the compiler's secret guard requires — and network_id from networkconf_id, which no name match would have found. site is provider-owned rather than the SDK's site_id, set from a parameter in accountToModel. Eleven of the sixteen SDK fields are omitted, including filter_ids, ip and ulp_user_id, none of which the released schema exposed. unifi_account serves this same schema through its deprecated alias, so its fifteen behaviour-inventory lines are the check that the alias still inherits what it did. Admission waits on a campaign run.
